completion_data.completion_summary: Built context-reachability.sh, a standing source-store probe computing three non-short-circuiting reachability styles (filename/directory/index) plus eager/lazy classification over the 591-file context corpus, registered it in manifest.json and the utility-scripts inventory, documented directory-reference reachability in context-discovery.md, and closed the removal decision gate with an empty confirmed-dead set (Reasoned Exclusions) per the research's own prediction.

memory_candidates.content: When batching reachability/caller-census grep checks over a few-hundred-file corpus, a naive per-candidate `grep -r` loop (one invocation per candidate, times N candidates, times M sub-patterns each) re-scans the whole corpus hundreds or thousands of times and can take minutes. Replace with a two-pass batched design: collect every distinct pattern (basename, directory suffix, etc.) across all candidates ONCE into a patterns file, run exactly ONE multi-pattern `grep -Ho -f patterns_file` pass over the corpus producing "path:match" lines, then look up each candidate's own pattern(s) against the resulting map in a second, pure-bash pass. Cuts a 5-minute probe to ~30-40s on a 591-file / 4.7MB corpus.

A reachability check over directory-reference agent-prose conventions must test every contiguous sub-range of a candidate's directory-component list, not only ranges ending at the file's own leaf directory. A bare reference to an ANCESTOR directory (e.g. 'deck/contents/' with no per-subdirectory mention at all) covers every file beneath it transitively via subtree inheritance; a leaf-anchored-only suffix design silently misses this and produces false-orphan findings for exactly the files whose only reference is at a shallower directory level.
